md.areas: south-central New Mexico and far west Texas
md.summary: Threat for large hail, severe wind, and perhaps a brief tornado continues within WW696.
md.discussion: Supercells continue across southern New Mexico this afternoon, with several splits and supercell mergers ongoing. VAD profiles from ABX and EPZ depict linear and elongated hodographs, supporting continued splitting supercells. Winds aloft veer to southwesterly just off the surface. Surface observations near the Rio Grande Valley are more southeasterly. If the supercells/supercell clusters west of El Paso can deviate more strongly eastward, a slight increase in low-level SRH and potential for a tornado where dew points are near 50 F. Moisture becomes more limited with eastern and northern extent where dew points are more around the mid 40s F. Overall, the main threats will likely remain large hail and severe wind.

Skill decays with lead - treat week 3-4 and monthly as trends, not weather.
